html:
The Church of Cyprus is the Orthodox church of the island, founded according to tradition by the apostles Paul and Barnabas around 45 CE and recognised as self governing by the Council of Ephesus in 431.

The Patriarch of Antioch claimed authority over it, but the council upheld its independence. In 488 the emperor Zeno confirmed it after the bones of Barnabas were found, and gave its archbishop the right to sign in red ink and carry a sceptre. Under Latin and Ottoman rule the archbishop became the ethnarch, the leader of the Greek Cypriots. That role passed into politics with Archbishop Makarios, first president of Cyprus.
sum: The Church of Cyprus is the Orthodox church of the island, founded according to tradition by the apostles Paul and Barnabas around 45 CE and recognised as self governing by the Council of Ephesus in 431.
